instruction: Check the research papers spreadsheet on my desktop, identify the most recently published paper, and save its title in a Word file called 'latest_paper.docx' in /home/user.

rules.title: TinyBERT: Distilling BERT for Natural Language Understanding

metadata.explanation: Task requires identifying the most recently published paper from the spreadsheet (rows 1-5 contain papers). Verified with Python: 'TinyBERT: Distilling BERT for Natural Language Understanding' (2019/9/23) is the latest among BERT (2018/10/11), Attention (2017/6/12), GLUE (2018/4/20), and ELMo (2018/2/15). The evaluator checks if the created DOCX file contains this paper title.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly checks if the DOCX file contains the expected paper title 'TinyBERT: Distilling BERT for Natural Language Understanding'
The expected title value is semantically correct - it is indeed the most recent paper (2019/9/23) among the 5 papers in the spreadsheet
Getter logic is correct: extracts text content from /home/user/latest_paper.docx using python-docx library
Metric logic is correct: performs case-insensitive substring search for the title in the document content
Evaluator will correctly pass if user completes task (writes correct title) and fail if user writes wrong title
However, design is suboptimal: xlsx getter function exists but is unused - evaluator uses hardcoded expected value instead of dynamically reading spreadsheet at eval time
Current approach assumes static spreadsheet content and won't adapt if data changes, though for this specific task with fixed download URL this is acceptable
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using the xlsx getter to dynamically determine the latest paper at evaluation time instead of hardcoding the expected title
Modify evaluator to: (1) Use get_xlsx_latest_paper__fca57ed0800553851d5057d288f20b50 to extract latest paper from spreadsheet, (2) Compare latest paper's title against DOCX content
This would make the evaluator more robust and would properly verify that the spreadsheet analysis logic itself is correct, not just the final output
